info.name: pf ecosystem
info.description: All pf-* services in one collection: pf-rates, pf-svc-income, pf-sheets. pf-db is DDL/migrations only and exposes no HTTP API. Managed as JSON in pf-postman -- see the pf-postman README for how edits here sync to your real Postman workspace.

item.name: pf-rates

request.description: Batch lookup; each result preserves its input pair and may return null when the value is unavailable. Maximum 500 pairs.
Batch lookup; each result preserves its input pair and may return null when the value is unavailable. Maximum 500 pairs.
Renamed from /currencies -- returns both fiat currencies (is_fiat=true, unit_kind=currency) and index units like UF/UTM (is_fiat=false, unit_kind=index_unit); see pf-rates/docs/api.md.
No auth required.

item.name: pf-svc-income

request.description: Atomic batch: contracts require a persisted employer_id and started_at.
Atomic batch: omit id to create; include an existing id to update. Do not use this request as a negative-test fixture.
Operational deletion by stable IDs. Use only with IDs whose dependency guards permit deletion.
Operational deletion by stable IDs. Use only with IDs whose dependency guards permit deletion.
Lists contracts as { id, employer: { id, name }, started_at, ended_at, is_indefinite, position, is_in_effect }. is_in_effect reflects today's date within the contract interval.
Lists employers with nested contracts. Each nested contract contains id, started_at, ended_at, is_indefinite, position, and is_in_effect; the employer is not repeated.
No auth required.

Blank, header-only spreadsheet shell (zero data rows) with the exact wide-format column headers POST /payroll/import/spreadsheet expects -- never reads the database. Fill it in by hand, then send it to Import Spreadsheet above.

Bulk-exports every persisted period matching the (optional, disabled by default) employer/period_year/period_month filters -- omitting all three exports every persisted period. Includes two extra computed-only columns (income_tax, unemployment_insurance) that Import Spreadsheet silently ignores on re-import, so exporting and re-importing this exact file back through 'Import Spreadsheet (mode=validate)' is safe and idempotent for every other column.

exec: // Chains off 'Preview a PDF payslip': wraps whatever that request's
// Tests script stashed into last_pdf_preview_response into a valid
// { mode, periods } body -- run the preview request at least once first.
throw new Error("No stashed preview found -- run 'Preview a PDF payslip' first (its Tests script saves the response into 'last_pdf_preview_response').");
// mode comes from the 'import_json_mode' collection variable so you can
// flip commit/validate from the Postman variable list -- no script
// editing needed. Defaults to 'validate' if unset/blank, on purpose: a
// chained import must never silently persist real payroll data.
pm.request.body.raw = JSON.stringify({ mode: mode, periods: periods }, null, 2);

request.description: Same endpoint as 'Import JSON (mode=validate)', but the body is built entirely from the last 'Preview a PDF payslip' response by this request's Pre-request Script -- run that request first (with one or more PDFs attached), then run this one to validate the extracted payrolls without retyping anything. Sends whatever mode is set in the 'import_json_mode' collection variable, defaulting to 'validate' when that variable is empty/unset -- set 'import_json_mode' to 'commit' in the collection's variable list when you actually want to persist; no script editing needed.

validate runs the real pipeline then rolls back; unresolved_rows in the response lists rows with concept_code=null (identified by period_index + row_index). periods must have at least one element, and no two elements may share the same (employer, period_year, period_month). Resend with mode=commit once resolved.
mode form field defaults to "commit" when omitted -- send mode=validate to preview reconciliation conflicts for the whole file without persisting anything (see pf-svc-income/docs/api.md).

exec: // Stash the raw preview array so 'Import JSON (from last Preview)' can
// wrap it into a { mode, periods } body without any copy/pasting.

request.description: Read-only, never persists -- deliberately not under /payroll/import/*, since (unlike the two requests in the Import folder) this one never imports anything, it just converts one or more PDF payslips into a JSON array of previews (one per file, in upload order). Add more 'files' form-data rows with the same key to preview a batch of distinct liquidaciones in one request. See docs/payroll-workflow.md.

Same unified nested shape (id/employer/period/amount) as one item of 'List payrolls' above, filtered to this period_id. Unlike that endpoint, not bound by any previous_months/future_months window -- works for any historical period_id. 404 if not found.

query.description: Any non-negative integer. Defaults to 12 (padded with inferred placeholders if history is shorter). Passing this explicitly -- even as 12 -- disables that padding; only payrolls genuinely in the database are returned.
Non-negative, capped at 12 (422 above that). Defaults to 12.

request.description: Unifies the former separate Period range / Period summaries endpoints -- each item nests its temporal identity under 'period' ({year, month, date_range: {start, end}, timeframe: previous|current|future}) and its financial figures under 'amount' (gross_income_clp, taxable_income_clp, total_discounts_clp, net_pay_clp, net_pay_uf, net_pay_usd, net_pay_eur, increase, net_pay_clp_today); only a top-level 'id' and a nested employer object ({id, name}, null as a whole for synthetic entries) live outside those two buckets.

item.name: Templates

request.description: employer_id is required -- the employer must already have a PAY_EMPLOYER row (i.e. its first payroll import has already run; there is no standalone endpoint to create one ahead of that). It is an admin-only FK -- matching against a real PDF only ever uses employer_match_pattern. There is no employer_name field: the response's employer_name is always resolved fresh from PAY_EMPLOYER.name at read time, never stored. Every regex (employer_match_pattern and each field's pdf_label_pattern) is compile-checked before reaching the database -- an invalid one is a 422. Fields have no kind -- the server always resolves it from PAY_CONCEPT via concept_code (an unknown concept_code is a 400, not a silent guess). Returns 201. A duplicate template_id is also a 400 (see pf-svc-income/docs/api.md).
Logical delete only -- sets is_active=false, never a row DELETE. A subsequent POST /payroll/pdf-preview no longer matches it, but Get one template still finds it. 404 if it doesn't exist.
Found regardless of is_active status -- a direct lookup by template_id always finds it. 404 if it never existed.

query.description: Set true to also list logically-deleted (is_active=false) templates.

request.description: Active-only by default.

Mutates the existing row in place -- does not create a new template_id/version (bump version in the body yourself if desired). Same body shape/validation as Create, minus template_id (taken from the path). 404 if it doesn't exist; 400 on the same constraint violations as Create.

item.description: Manages the versioned templates POST /payroll/pdf-preview matches PDFs against. Persisted in pf-db's PAY_PDF_TEMPLATE/PAY_PDF_TEMPLATE_FIELD tables, not a git-tracked file -- see https://github.com/mrturo-pf/pf-improvements/blob/main/improvements/HIST-019-pdf-template-management/recommendation.md.
See modules/pf-svc-income/docs/api.md for the full reference.

variable.description: Auto-populated by 'Preview a PDF payslip's Tests script; consumed by 'Import JSON (from last Preview)'s Pre-request Script. Never edit by hand.

Consumed by 'Import JSON (from last Preview)'s Pre-request Script to pick the request's mode -- set to 'commit' here (in the variable list, not the script) when you actually want the chained import to persist. Defaults to 'validate' for safety; leave it that way unless you mean it.
